pairs.question: Quid ergo inter duo interest?
pairs.answer: Honestum est perfectum bonum, quo beata uita completur, cuius contactu alia quoque bona fiunt.
pairs.derivation: Seneca asks himself the difference between bonum and honestum (Quid ergo inter duo interest?) and answers directly with the definition of honestum. Answer ends at the first full stop; what follows (Quod dico talest...) begins a new illustrative point.

pairs.question: Unde adcognoscitur bonum?
pairs.derivation: Authorial question (Unde adcognoscitur bonum?) immediately answered by the conditional clause. Capitalized initial Si; answer ends at the full stop, after which an imagined interlocutor speaks ('Fateris' inquis...).

pairs.question: Quare autem bonum in arbore animalique muto non est?
pairs.derivation: Seneca poses the question and answers it himself in the same sentence (quia nec ratio). Answer is the contiguous elliptical clause; what follows (Ob hoc in infante quoque non est...) extends the point to infants.
